backing_regression.scope: Actual image-sized whole-owner reserve/zero/erase/release, with read-only hardware-breakpoint observations; no protected activation

boot_binding.scope: Fresh complete private adapter/kernel reconstruction and retained-role identities; no activation, CPU lifetime or production publication

component.scope: Private inactive-preparation direct-call closure and conservative normal boot-stack bound; fatal recovery and production publication excluded

limitations: Firmware inventory and CPU boundary snapshots do not establish startup, parking, scheduling, hotplug, asynchronous exclusion or continuous lifetime.
Retained decoding establishes internal snapshot consistency, not atomic firmware capture or future firmware ownership.
Native firmware uses the legacy RSDP/RSDT path; XSDT, online-capable/unusable processor records, unsupported formats and malformed-state refusals have model coverage only in this matrix.
Altered records, corrected-checksum firmware bytes and read checkpoints are offline controls, not guest-state injection or native failure execution.
Prepared banks remain inactive and are erased/released; complete active/restorable root, alias, writer, effective-mode and publication/lifetime integration remains required.
The historical full compiler suite, its host-RWX/injected-state cases and the 51-workload third-party corpus were not rerun for this snapshot.
The compact receipt is not a closed source archive or a production publisher proof.
Full Linux UAPI, DTS, distribution, Docker/Podman and VM-host acceptance remain incomplete.
